investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time; the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because no pod could be placed, createAgent() never returned a VM identity, and the eval runner could not populate any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap and a fail status on all three sibling checks.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: pod was stuck unscheduled for 132s before the check timed out at latencyMs=140225, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the pod never started.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed under missingRequiredEvidence.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: contract gap covers all four required fields — orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState — confirming zero successful output was produced.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck for 142s, empty evidenceKeys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck for 147s, empty evidenceKeys.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never returned because the pod was never scheduled, so no evidence was written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so any capacity shortfall on those nodes is total; if the selector is overly narrow it could exclude otherwise eligible nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, meaning the cluster has a small blast radius for this resource type; a modest increase in demand saturates it entirely.

Quaternary — leaked or non-terminated remote agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup() failed to delete a previous agent, its VM slot would remain allocated and unavailable to new pods.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible Kubernetes nodes to determine whether slots are exhausted by active workloads, leaked eval pods, or both.

Audit all remote-agent pods in the cluster namespace for any that are in Terminating, Pending, or zombie states and manually delete them to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots if withCleanup() failed to reclaim them.

After freeing capacity, re-run the remote-agent-create eval to confirm the scheduler can place the pod and that all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are produced.

Evaluate whether the cluster needs additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval runs and production workloads without exhaustion; only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource, creating a narrow scheduling target.

Review the pod's node affinity and selector configuration to determine whether it can be safely broadened to include additional nodes, reducing the risk of total scheduling failure when the 2 eligible nodes are saturated.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If capacity has been freed, a passing run producing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent=true, and remoteState in ['running','idle','ready'] would confirm the failure was capacity-driven and is now resolved.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity and selector on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If the selector is overly restrictive, widening it could expose more schedulable nodes and reduce the blast radius of future exhaustion events.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec used by createAgent() for machineType='remote' and verify that the node affinity/selector intentionally restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, or whether additional nodes should be eligible.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a misconfigured node selector or affinity rule should be investigated instead.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released slots) rather than a sustained capacity problem.
If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes, the root cause would be a configuration change rather than resource exhaustion.
If the two kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes were cordoned, drained, or in a NotReady state at the time of the failure, the cause would be node unavailability rather than resource slot exhaustion.
If no prior eval run leaked VMs and all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are accounted for by legitimate workloads, the cause is under-provisioning rather than a cleanup failure.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and emit a warning if headroom falls below a minimum threshold.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods are left in Terminating or zombie states after each eval run, catching withCleanup() failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-readiness eval for the remote-agents feature that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node has available capacity, surfacing infrastructure saturation independently of the agent creation flow.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to record the scheduler rejection message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerReason, eligibleNodeCount, insufficientResourceNodes) so future failures produce diagnostic evidence rather than an empty evidence object.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T12:53–12:58Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the remote-agent-state expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not match the affinity/selector at all. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted by the eval runner (and by extension any real remote-agent creation request) is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the agent pod never starts, the runner cannot collect the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) mandated by the remote-agent-state expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.

Preemption is also unavailable (no victims found), so the scheduler cannot free slots.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the remote-agent eval probes was left in Unschedulable state for 130–150 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected signal, and no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message is explicit about the resource type and node count.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared VM scheduling layer is the common dependency.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new peer-pod VMs, and preemption found no evictable victims, meaning existing workloads are holding all slots.

[Likely secondary] The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules (e.g., a label such as kata-containers=true or a specific node pool label is absent), permanently excluding them from scheduling consideration regardless of VM capacity.
[Possible] The kata peer-pods node pool has been scaled down or a node has become NotReady, reducing the eligible node count below what is needed to absorb current demand.
[Possible] A long-running or leaked remote-agent VM from a prior eval or user session is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and was not cleaned up, exhausting the quota.

[Lower confidence] A configuration change in the cluster (node labels, resource limits, or affinity rules) may have reduced the effective scheduling surface, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time; the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because no pod could be placed, createAgent() never returned a VM identity, and the eval runner could not populate any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap and a fail status on all three sibling checks.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: pod was stuck unscheduled for 132s before the check timed out at latencyMs=140225, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the pod never started.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed under missingRequiredEvidence.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: contract gap covers all four required fields — orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState — confirming zero successful output was produced.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck for 142s, empty evidenceKeys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck for 147s, empty evidenceKeys.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never returned because the pod was never scheduled, so no evidence was written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so any capacity shortfall on those nodes is total; if the selector is overly narrow it could exclude otherwise eligible nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, meaning the cluster has a small blast radius for this resource type; a modest increase in demand saturates it entirely.

Quaternary — leaked or non-terminated remote agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup() failed to delete a previous agent, its VM slot would remain allocated and unavailable to new pods.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a misconfigured node selector or affinity rule should be investigated instead.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released slots) rather than a sustained capacity problem.
If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes, the root cause would be a configuration change rather than resource exhaustion.
If the two kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes were cordoned, drained, or in a NotReady state at the time of the failure, the cause would be node unavailability rather than resource slot exhaustion.
If no prior eval run leaked VMs and all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are accounted for by legitimate workloads, the cause is under-provisioning rather than a cleanup failure.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and emit a warning if headroom falls below a minimum threshold.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods are left in Terminating or zombie states after each eval run, catching withCleanup() failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-readiness eval for the remote-agents feature that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node has available capacity, surfacing infrastructure saturation independently of the agent creation flow.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to record the scheduler rejection message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerReason, eligibleNodeCount, insufficientResourceNodes) so future failures produce diagnostic evidence rather than an empty evidence object.

[Likely secondary] The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules (e.g., a label such as kata-containers=true or a specific node pool label is absent), permanently excluding them from scheduling consideration regardless of VM capacity.
[Possible] The kata peer-pods node pool has been scaled down or a node has become NotReady, reducing the eligible node count below what is needed to absorb current demand.
[Possible] A long-running or leaked remote-agent VM from a prior eval or user session is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and was not cleaned up, exhausting the quota.

[Lower confidence] A configuration change in the cluster (node labels, resource limits, or affinity rules) may have reduced the effective scheduling surface, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

reproductionSteps.details: Run kubectl get pods -A -o wide and filter for pods using the kata runtime class to identify any leaked or long-running VMs holding capacity.

reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the pod spec submitted by the eval probe (or the agent creation API) and confirm which node labels are required, then verify those labels exist on the 4 excluded nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — kata peer-pod VM scheduling layer
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes eligible by affinity, blocking all remote-agent pod creation. This is the earliest violated boundary in the eval execution path.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded from scheduling by the pod's node affinity or selector rules, reducing the effective VM pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity exhaustion.

affectedAreas.label: Eval check: remote-agent-state (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check failed at 12:55:34Z with the same Unschedulable message (evidence id: sibling.remote-agent-state), confirming the VM pool was still exhausted across sequential eval runs.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm resource utilization on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine if the pool is still exhausted.
Identify and clean up any leaked or orphaned remote-agent VMs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads.
Evaluate whether the node affinity/selector rules can be relaxed or whether additional nodes can be labeled to expand the eligible scheduling pool beyond 2 nodes.
Consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or scaling the kata peer-pods node pool if demand regularly approaches current limits.

Review the remote-agents feature registry configuration (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 183–188): degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 mean two required-check failures (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) already meet the outage threshold — confirm whether the feature health status has been updated accordingly.
Add a pre-flight eval or alerting rule that monitors kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on eligible nodes and fires before the pool is fully exhausted, enabling proactive remediation.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe to confirm failure is still present
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Establishes whether the scheduling failure is sustained or was transient at the time of the original run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the 2 kata-eligible nodes to inspect VM resource capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Will show kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs. current Requests, directly confirming or disproving the resource exhaustion hypothesis. Replace <kata-affinity-label> with the actual node selector label from the pod spec.

recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.runtimeClassName=="kata-remote" or .spec.runtimeClassName=="kata-cc")'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any long-running or leaked remote-agent VMs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect the pod spec submitted by the eval probe to confirm node affinity rules
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms which node labels are required and whether the 4 excluded nodes could ever be made eligible by label changes or affinity rule updates.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pending or failed pod spec from the remote-agents namespace and examine its nodeAffinity and nodeSelector fields.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared dependency
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the VM pool is the confirmed shared failure point. If only one fails, the diagnosis should be narrowed.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and not fully consumed, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.
If the failing pod spec does not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would need an alternative explanation (e.g., a misconfigured resource quota or admission webhook).
If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are shown to actually match the pod's required labels, the node affinity hypothesis would be disproved and the cluster topology would need re-examination.
If a subsequent eval run passes without any infrastructure change, the failure may have been transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent VM requests) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes while remote-agent-runtime fails, the shared VM scheduling dependency hypothesis would be weakened and a runtime-specific issue would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested on eligible nodes and fails with a warning before the pool reaches 100% utilization.
Add a remote-agent-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned or leaked remote-agent VMs persist beyond a configurable TTL, catching resource leaks before they exhaust the scheduling pool.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 3), alerting if the eligible pool shrinks due to node failures or label changes.

Extend the existing remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence when scheduling fails, enabling faster triage without requiring manual kubectl inspection.
